Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 99, verses 1–8:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Idha zulzilati al-ardu﴾: That is, it shakes for the establishment of the Hour.

﴿Wa akhrajati al-ardu athqalaha﴾: That is, its treasures and its dead; it casts them out and empties itself.

﴿Ma laha﴾: That is, the disbelieving human says, "What is wrong with it?" That is, what made it shake with this shaking?

﴿Tuhaddithu akhbaraha﴾: That is, it informs of what happened upon it of good and evil, and bears witness to it for its people.

﴿Awha laha﴾: That is, that it should relate its news, so it related.

﴿Yasduru al-nasu ashtatan﴾: That is, from the place of reckoning.

﴿Liyaw a'malahum﴾: That is, the recompense of their deeds, either to Paradise or to Hell.

﴿Mithqala dharratin﴾: The weight of a small ant.

Meaning of the verses:

The Most High said, ﴿When the earth is shaken with its violent shaking﴾, meaning it shakes its intense shaking for the establishment of the Hour, and the earth casts out its burdens, of treasures, and of the dead; the treasures are at the first blast, and the dead are at the second blast. So in the report there is brevity, since the intent is to establish resurrection and recompense, so that people act by what saves them from the Fire and admits them to Paradise.

And His saying, ﴿And man says, "What is wrong with it?"﴾ There is no doubt that this questioning human was a disbeliever in the Hour, and therefore he asked. As for the believer, he knows this, because it is part of his creed. And His saying, ﴿On that Day it will relate its news﴾, meaning it informs of what happened upon it of good and evil, by tongue of speech or by state. In this reporting it is commanded, by His saying, ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾, meaning, to that effect. And His saying, ﴿On that Day mankind will depart in scattered groups﴾, meaning on the day the earth is shaken and quakes for the second blast, a blast by which people depart in scattered groups, that is, they depart from the courtyard of the judgment of decision, so some take the right path and some take the left path, ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾, that is, the recompense of their deeds in the world, of good and evil. Good deeds bequeath Paradise and evil deeds bequeath the Fire. And His saying, the Most High, ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾, meaning the weight of an atom of good in the world, he will be rewarded for it in the Hereafter; and whoever does an atom's weight of evil in the world will be repaid for it in the Hereafter, unless the Mighty and Majestic Compeller pardons him. Since disbelief prevents entry into Paradise, when the disbeliever does a good deed in the world he sees its recompense in the world, and he has nothing of it in the Hereafter. This is based on the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, when she asked the Messenger ﷺ about 'Abdullah ibn Jud'an, whether what he used to do in the world, of feeding pilgrims and clothing them, would benefit him in the Hereafter. He said to her: "No, for he never once said, 'My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment.'" Likewise, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, was eating with the Messenger ﷺ when this verse was revealed: "Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it," and Abu Bakr raised his hand from the food and said, "Indeed I will see what I did of good and evil?" The Prophet ﷺ said, "What you see of what you dislike is from the atoms of evil, and much evil; and Allah stores for you the atoms of good until you are given them on the Day of Resurrection." Confirmation of this is in the Book of Allah: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [al-Shura: 30].

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing the creed of resurrection and recompense.

2- Informing of the cosmic transformation in which the earth becomes other than the earth and the heavens other than the heavens.

3- Inanimate things speaking is among the signs of Allah the Most High that indicate His power, knowledge and wisdom, and these are the requirements of His divinity, by worshipping Him alone without any other.

3- Affirmation of the authentic hadith: "Protect yourselves from the Fire even with half a date."

5- The disbeliever's good deeds benefit him in the world but not in the Hereafter.

6- The believer is recompensed for an evil deed in the world, and his righteous deeds are stored for him for the Hereafter.

In this reporting it is commanded, by His saying, ﴿Because your Lord has inspired it﴾, meaning, to that effect. And His saying, ﴿On that Day mankind will depart in scattered groups﴾, meaning on the day the earth is shaken and quakes for the second blast, a blast by which people depart in scattered groups, that is, they depart from the courtyard of the judgment of decision, so some take the right path and some take the left path, ﴿to be shown their deeds﴾, that is, the recompense of their deeds in the world, of good and evil. Good deeds bequeath Paradise and evil deeds bequeath the Fire. And His saying, the Most High, ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾, meaning the weight of an atom of good in the world, he will be rewarded for it in the Hereafter; and whoever does an atom's weight of evil in the world will be repaid for it in the Hereafter, unless the Mighty and Majestic Compeller pardons him. Since disbelief prevents entry into Paradise, when the disbeliever does a good deed in the world he sees its recompense in the world, and he has nothing of it in the Hereafter. This is based on the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, when she asked the Messenger ﷺ about 'Abdullah ibn Jud'an, whether what he used to do in the world, of feeding pilgrims and clothing them, would benefit him in the Hereafter. He said to her: "No, for he never once said, 'My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment.'" The Prophet ﷺ said, "What you see of what you dislike is from the atoms of evil, and much evil; and Allah stores for you the atoms of good until you are given them on the Day of Resurrection." Confirmation of this is in the Book of Allah: ﴿And whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [al-Shura: 30].

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Establishing the creed of resurrection and recompense.

2- Informing of the cosmic transformation in which the earth becomes other than the earth and the heavens other than the heavens.

3- Inanimate things speaking is among the signs of Allah the Most High that indicate His power, knowledge and wisdom, and these are the requirements of His divinity, by worshipping Him alone without any other.

3- Affirmation of the authentic hadith: "Protect yourselves from the Fire even with half a date."

5- The disbeliever's good deeds benefit him in the world but not in the Hereafter.

6- The believer is recompensed for an evil deed in the world, and his righteous deeds are stored for him for the Hereafter.
